requirement: Rapid voltage change at the PoC on the AI-training load step
source: EU RfG (2016/631) and DCC (2016/1388), Continental Europe: not set by RfG/DCC; IEC TR 61000-3-7 indicative planning levels for infrequent rapid voltage changes at HV/EHV are about 3-5 % (not verified against the text here); 3 % used
note: Voltage change on the voltage form (cos ψ·ΔP + sin ψ·ΔQ)/S_k, ψ = atan(X/R), IEC TR 61000-3-7: ΔP 23.4 MW, ΔQ 2.34 Mvar (tan φ_swing 0.1 from the envelope), X/R 4 (assumed; typical grid X/R, replace with the network operator's value) gives 3.178 %; the X/R-free bound √(ΔP² + ΔQ²)/S_k is 9.407 %; for reference the P-only ΔS/S_k = 23.4 MW / 250 MVA = 9.36 %; S_k is the entered S_k'' with the IEC 60909 c factor, so d may be understated by up to 1.1; above the limit a power-flow or EMT study is needed; the AI-training load is read at the point of connection before any UPS or battery smoothing, so the verdict is before mitigation, not final

after_battery.note: 2030: of the 23.4 MW step, batteries hold 0 MW to the 4 MW/min limit; the UPS walks 23.4 MW in over 15 s (93.6 MW/min); the uncovered part (0 MW) is counted at the envelope's rate, conservatively, and a 0 MW oscillation remains; short by the smoothing screen: a 23.4 MW step through the 4 MW/min limit takes 5.85 min and 1.14 MWh each way; oscillation 3.4 MW above the limit, 0.0006 MWh of swing; need 26.8 MW / 2.28 MWh against 40 MW / 3.75 MWh left after backup; UPS ups_battery: 5.75 MWh kept to bridge 34.5 MW for 600 s; 'ups_battery' walks in over 15 s (UPS, assumed); closed form on the envelope's phases, blind to in-hour ramps beyond them; energies as delivered, charging losses not added; the UPS carries 23.4 MW of the step and walks it onto the grid over 15 s, 93.6 MW/min, above the 4 MW/min limit; bess_new sized by the run, not counted
